text:
nightly-bot: Nightly eval failed for model redwood-v2-quant-int4 on promptset 'reasoning-short'. Quality drop: BLEU -12%, sample entropy -1.2 bits, repetition rate 54%. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood.ai/evals/1876549876 :eyes:
ana: saw it, on it.
rahul: this the INT4 job we rolled yesterday?
maria: yes, rolled quantized kernels at 2026-03-17 03:12UTC (commit c3f4a9b). No other model code changes.
jon: i can repro quickly with nightly config — sampling looks collapsed, many repeated tokens even though temp=0.9.
lucy: hosted inference logs looked normal for the same model earlier today, which points to the eval harness or postproc.
sam: dumping raw logits from harness run now (`--dump-logits /tmp/logits.npy`).
rahul: can you also run fp16 vs int4 with the same seed? want to see if quantization or harness is the culprit.
nana: started fp16 job with same seed 12345.
jon: attaching short snippet from the harness sample (int4):
```
prompt: "What causes the seasons?"
seed: 12345
temperature: 0.9
sampled: "the the the the the"
logit_snapshot: top10_probs [0.92,0.03,0.01,0.01,0.01,...]
```
maria: those top probs look suspicious; quantized logits seem artificially peaked. but why only in harness?
lucy: harness recently changed RNG seeding when we moved to parallel workers (PR 2248). maybe seeding interaction with quantized kernels?
eval-harness-bot: test-matrix: sampling-seed-stability (workers=8) completed with warnings: correlated-seeds detected.
rahul: correlated seeds would cause low effective entropy if workers start similar states. can we grep for seed width? maybe using 32-bit seeds truncated.
maria: digging into PR 2248: we switched to numpy.default_rng().integers for per-worker seeds, but cast to int32 before passing to the C PRNG bridge. some PRNGs expect 64-bit -> truncation risk.
sam: i re-ran with explicit 64-bit seeds and the int4 run's entropy recovered to parity with fp16.
nana: nice. so harness seed truncation into 32-bit was the proximate cause. any idea why that manifests more strongly with quantized kernels?
jon: quantization reduces dynamic range; coupled with correlated RNG states, sampling noise is insufficient to overcome a few dominant logits => collapse.
lucy: conclusion: two-factor issue: (1) seed width truncation in harness, (2) quantized kernel's lower entropy amplification. fix both where feasible.
maria: opened PR #2359 to preserve 64-bit seeds through the C bridge and to add a guard/assert. link: https://git.internal/redwood/PR/2359
ana: can we hotfix harness on nightly branch and re-run tonight?
rahul: i'll cherry-pick #2359 to nightly branch and kick off a rebuild. also adding a small unit test: sample_entropy(seed=range(1,20)) mean > 2.0 bits for reasoning-short.
sam: re-run logs look good locally after patch: BLEU restored, entropy delta ~+1.3 bits vs failing run.
john (typo: jon): can we also add monitoring to alert if entropy delta > 0.5 bits vs baseline for any model?
lucy: yes, add to console -> per-model quality regression metric. i'll file a task.
maria: we'll also add a harness-only check that warns if seeds appear highly correlated across workers (simple pairwise overlap metric).
nana: thanks everyone. i'll update the incident board and mark blocked->in-progress->resolved after nightly finishes.
rahul: followups: backfill the failing nightly with fixed harness and add postmortem notes to eng-ml.
nana: adding to changelog and release notes: "fix: preserve 64-bit RNG seeds in harness to avoid sampling collapse with quantized kernels".
lucy: great catch. :tada:
sam: leaving a comment on PR to add extra unit for int4 sampling behavior.
eval-harness-bot: job 1876553001 completed: nightly-eval (with patch) shows metrics within expected bounds.
nana: closing thread once nightly finishes and metrics look stable. thanks all for fast triage.
